rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, the maximum annual rent increase is 1.6% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027. Multiply base rent by .016 to get the maximum dollar increase.
rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the current allowable-increase period announced Jan 14, 2026; the rate is adjusted each March 1 (prior period 1.4%). Underlying ordinance date not stated in documents.

unverifiable_exemptions: Units built after June 13, 1979 and Costa-Hawkins exemptions (e.g., single-family homes, condos) cannot be verified from parcel data

rules.review_note: Documents do not state construction cutoff for rent-control coverage; cutoff not applied.

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance just cause eviction and relocation payments
rules.requirement: A landlord of a unit covered by the Rent Ordinance may evict only for one of 17 listed just causes, which must be the dominant motive. For no-fault evictions the landlord must pay relocation (notices served 3/1/2026–2/28/2027: $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly/disabled tenant or household with a minor child; Ellis Act evictions $11,110.05 per tenant, max $33,330.13, plus $7,443.90).
rules.key_value: 17 enumerated just causes; relocation $8,245 per tenant, max $24,733 per unit (Ellis Act: $11,110.05, max $33,330.13)
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance; also covers some tenancies exempt from the rent increase limits (post-June 13, 1979 CO units, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, some government-regulated tenancies).
rules.penalty: Landlord who evicts or tries to evict unlawfully may face substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.exemptions: Temporary capital improvement evictions of less than 20 days are governed by Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9 for relocation, not § 37.9C.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction
rules.effective_date_note: Documents give no effective date for the just cause provisions; relocation rates in the key value apply from 2026-03-01 and adjust each March 1.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancies in units regulated by other government agencies may be exempt
owner-occupancy and other exemptions under the Rent Ordinance

rules.review_note: Relocation schedules (D082, D083) folded into this record; § 37.9C and § 37.9A section numbers come from the Rent Board rate pages.

rules.title: SF security deposit interest rate
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on tenant security deposits at 4.2% for March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027; the rate is reset each March 1.
citation_aliases: SF Rent Board security deposit interest rate
rules.quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.effective_date_note: Start of the rate period stated in the document.
rules.review_note: The document does not cite the code section for the interest requirement; cited by chapter only.

rules.title: SF Rent Ordinance ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords and vendors may not sell or use algorithmic devices that analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend rents or manage occupancy. Tenants or the City Attorney can sue; remedies include damages, injunctions and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with each unit-month a separate violation.
rules.key_value: ban on algorithmic devices using nonpublic competitor data; up to $1,000 per violation
rules.penalty: Damages, injunctive relief, civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each month per affected unit may be a separate violation
rules.quoted_span: The law prohibits the sale or use of such algorithmic devices and allows a tenant or the City Attorney to bring a civil action if they believe an entity is in violation of the law
rules.effective_date_note: Official SF.gov page says it went into effect October 14, 2024; law firm alert says only 'October 2024'.

rules.title: SF Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
rules.key_value: protection for people with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing
rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.

requires_unknown_facts: unit is in an affordable housing project

rules.review_note: Only a short agency landing page; section citation not stated.

parsed.notes: Merged duplicate rent, algorithmic, and relocation records. Relocation schedules folded into the just cause record. No San Francisco-specific application-fee rule appears in the documents (state Civ. Code § 1950.6 applies).
